title.en: US launches seventh night of Iran strikes as Hormuz conflict escalates
title.zh: 美国对伊朗发动第七晚袭击，霍尔木兹冲突升级

summary.en: US Central Command announced a seventh consecutive night of strikes on Iran, stating the attacks were intended to degrade Iranian military capabilities as conflict escalates over the Strait of Hormuz.
summary.zh: 美国中央司令部宣布，美军已连续第七晚对伊朗发动袭击，称这些袭击旨在随着霍尔木兹海峡冲突升级，继续削弱伊朗的军事能力。

body.en:
The US military said it had launched a seventh consecutive night of strikes on Iran on Friday night as fighting escalated over the strait of Hormuz.

US Central Command, in a post on X, said the strikes, which began at 7pm GMT, were designed to “continue degrading Iranian military capabilities”.

Iranian media reported explosions heard or strikes carried out in the cities of Sirik, Ahvaz and Yazd.

And late on Friday night Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said two oil tankers had hit mines in Hormuz and exploded. The US military said that claim was false.

The conflict continued on Saturday, with the IRCC saying it targeted ⁠a ⁠site where ​US combat aircraft ⁠were gathered at Sheikh Isa ⁠air base ​and ‌an ‌intelligence datacentre ‌in Bahrain known as Batelco, according to Iran’s state media.

The ‌IRGC reportedly also targeted a ​US naval fuel-support pier at al-⁠Ahmadi port and ​a US ​signals ​and communications ​centre ‌in Kuwait, while ⁠Kuwait temporarily suspended ‌operations at ‌its international airport because of Iranian missile and ‌drone attacks.

Earlier on Friday US airstrikes hit bridges in Iran’s southern Hormozgan province, killing at least seven people, Iranian state TV reported. The bridges were a key transit point for Bandar Abbas, Iran’s main port. Further US airstrikes brought down a tower in Chabahar port on the Gulf of Oman that the US military claimed the IRGC used to facilitate attacks on vessels in the strait of Hormuz. The US also targeted key electrical infrastructure and Iranshahr airport.

Iran’s energy ministry told citizens to reduce their use of electricity and air conditioning after the power grid came under strain due to US strikes on energy facilities. The ministry said areas in the south were experiencing “extreme heat and attacks on power infrastructure” as temperatures soared.

Strikes on civilian infrastructure not being used for military purposes could constitute a war crime, human rights experts have said.

Renewed US strikes had killed at least 38 people and wounded more than 400 in Iran by Friday morning, said a spokesperson for Iran’s health ministry, Hossein Kermanpour.

The attacks appeared to be the follow-through of Donald Trump’s promise to expand strikes against Iran, including the targeting of infrastructure and power plants. The US president reportedly met senior department heads this week to discuss an expanded aerial campaign to force Iran to reopen the strait of Hormuz.

The current round of fighting has entered its seventh day and further undermined the interim deal between Iran and the US, which was meant to keep the strait open and give room for negotiations to lead to a permanent truce. body.zh: 美国军方表示，随着霍尔木兹海峡的战斗升级，周五晚上对伊朗发动了连续第七晚的袭击。 美国中央司令部在 X 上发帖称，这次袭击于格林威治标准时间晚上 7 点开始，旨在“继续削弱伊朗的军事能力”。 伊朗媒体报道称，锡里克、阿瓦士和亚兹德等城市发生了爆炸或袭击事件。 周五深夜，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）表示，两艘油轮在霍尔木兹触雷并爆炸。美国军方表示，这一说法是错误的。 据伊朗官方媒体报道，冲突周六仍在继续，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队表示，袭击目标是谢赫伊萨空军基地美国战斗机聚集的地点以及巴林的一个名为 Batelco 的情报数据中心。 据报道，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队还瞄准了艾哈迈迪港的美国海军燃料支援码头和位于科威特的美国信号和通信中心，而由于伊朗导弹和无人机袭击，科威特暂时中止了其国际机场的运营。 据伊朗国家电视台报道，周五早些时候，美国空袭伊朗南部霍尔木兹甘省的桥梁，造成至少七人死亡。这些桥梁是伊朗主要港口阿巴斯港的重要中转站。美国的进一步空袭摧毁了阿曼湾恰巴哈尔港的一座塔楼，美国军方声称伊斯兰革命卫队利用该塔楼袭击霍尔木兹海峡的船只。美国还瞄准了关键的电力基础设施和伊朗沙赫尔机场。 由于美国对能源设施的袭击导致电网承受压力，伊朗能源部要求公民减少用电和空调的使用。该部表示，随着气温飙升，南部地区正在经历“酷热和对电力基础设施的攻击”。 人权专家表示，袭击不用于军事目的的民用基础设施可能构成战争罪。 伊朗卫生部发言人侯赛因·克尔曼普尔 (Hossein Kermanpour) 表示，截至周五上午，美国重新发动的空袭已在伊朗造成至少 38 人死亡、400 多人受伤。 这些袭击似乎是唐纳德·特朗普承诺扩大对伊朗的打击的后续行动，其中包括针对基础设施和发电厂。据报道，美国总统本周会见了高级部门负责人，讨论扩大空中打击行动，迫使伊朗重新开放霍尔木兹海峡。 本轮战斗已进入第七天，进一步破坏了伊朗和美国之间的临时协议，该协议旨在保持海峡开放并为谈判提供永久休战空间。伊朗关闭了海峡，美国重新封锁伊朗港口和船只...

reflection.en: The continuous cycle of strikes and counter-strikes highlights the enduring truth that violence often begets more violence. When nations take up the sword against one another, the path can quickly lead to deeper conflict and profound cost. Yahweh calls us to seek paths that break these cycles, rather than perpetuate them.
reflection.zh: 持续的打击与反击循环，凸显了暴力往往滋生更多暴力的持久真理。当国家彼此动武时，这条道路可能迅速导致更深的冲突和沉重的代价。雅伟呼召我们寻求打破这些循环的道路，而非使其持续下去。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

title.en: Amid elections, Sao Tome and Principe balances global powers
title.zh: 圣多美和普林西比在选举中平衡全球权力

summary.en: As voters head to the polls, Sao Tome and Principe is attracting international scrutiny. A military agreement with Russia has heightened interest in the strategically located archipelago.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As voters head to the polls, Sao Tome and Principe is attracting international scrutiny. A military agreement with Russia has heightened interest in the strategically located archipelago.

Voters in Sao Tome and Principe will elect a new president on Sunday, ahead of parliamentary elections at the end of September. For the island nation of just 245,000 people, the elections are a major domestic political event. They are also attracting growing international attention.

Since signing a military cooperation agreement with Russia in April 2024 , the archipelago in the Gulf of Guinea has attracted renewed geopolitical interest.

The key question is whether Russia is seeking to expand its influence in the South Atlantic through the archipelago — or whether the military agreement is largely symbolic, with Sao Tome and Principe merely continuing its long-standing foreign policy of maintaining ties with a wide range of international partners.

The former Portuguese colony  off the coast of Gabon and Equatorial Guinea marked the 51st anniversary of its independence on July 12. Although Sao Tome and Principe is one of Africa's smallest countries by both area and population, its location gives it strategic significance far beyond its size.

The archipelago lies on the equator in the Gulf of Guinea, a region crossed by major international shipping lanes and home to significant oil and gas reserves. At the same time, piracy, organized crime and the protection of maritime trade routes have turned the Gulf of Guinea into a key security hot spot.

"Sao Tome and Principe is a small country, but because of its geographical location in the Gulf of Guinea, it has enormous strategic importance," former Foreign Minister Elsa Pinto told DW.

"Major commercial and military routes pass through our waters. Even during the colonial era, our archipelago was of great importance because of its location between Africa and South America."

"Sao Tome was first a major center for sugar production, later the world's largest cocoa producer and also an important hub in the trans-Atlantic slave trade. That geostrategic importance has never disappeared."

Sao Tome and Principe drew international attention in the spring of 2024 after it emerged that the government had signed an open-ended military cooperation deal with Russia.

According to Russian officials, the agreement covers military training, technical assistance, cooperation on arms and military equipment, intelligence sharing and reciprocal visits by naval vessels and military aircraft. A separate accord was also signed between Russia's Interior Ministry and Sao Tome and Principe's national police force.

Coming amid Russia's war in Ukraine , the agreement was closely watched in Europe and the United States....
body.zh: 随着选民前往投票站，圣多美和普林西比正在吸引国际社会的关注。与俄罗斯达成的军事协议提高了人们对这个具有战略地位的群岛的兴趣。 圣多美和普林西比的选民将于周日在九月底的议会选举之前选出新总统。对于这个只有 245,000 人口的岛国来说，选举是一次重大的国内政治事件。它们也吸引了越来越多的国际关注。 自2024年4月与俄罗斯签署军事合作协议以来，几内亚湾群岛重新引起了地缘政治兴趣。 关键问题是，俄罗斯是否正在寻求通过该群岛扩大其在南大西洋的影响力，或者该军事协议是否在很大程度上具有象征意义，圣多美和普林西比只是继续其与广泛的国际伙伴保持关系的长期外交政策。 7 月 12 日，加蓬和赤道几内亚沿海的前葡萄牙殖民地庆祝其独立 51 周年。尽管圣多美和普林西比是非洲面积和人口最小的国家之一，但其地理位置赋予其战略意义远远超出其面积。 该群岛位于几内亚湾的赤道上，该地区有主要国际航道穿越，并且拥有大量石油和天然气储量。与此同时，海盗、有组织犯罪和海上贸易路线保护等问题已使几内亚湾成为重要的安全热点地区。 “圣多美和普林西比是一个小国，但由于其位于几内亚湾的地理位置，具有巨大的战略重要性，”前外交部长埃尔莎·平托告诉德国之声。 “主要的商业和军事路线都经过我们的水域。即使在殖民时代，我们的群岛也非常重要，因为它位于非洲和南美洲之间。” “圣多美首先是糖生产的主要中心，后来成为世界上最大的可可生产国，也是跨大西洋奴隶贸易的重要中心。这种地缘战略重要性从未消失。” 2024 年春天，圣多美和普林西比政府与俄罗斯签署了一项开放式军事合作协议，引起了国际社会的关注。 据俄罗斯官员称，该协议涵盖军事训练、技术援助、武器和军事装备合作、情报共享以及海军舰艇和军用飞机的互访。俄罗斯内政部与圣多美和普林西比国家警察部队还签署了一项单独协议。 在俄罗斯乌克兰战争之际，该协议受到欧洲和美国的密切关注……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to leadership, wisdom, and public responsibility. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with wisdom, integrity, and service, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

reflection.en: This report of a "furious clash" reminds us of the potent impact of words in public life. Proverbs 12:18 warns that "rash words are like sword thrusts," capable of inflicting deep wounds. May we strive for wisdom in our speech, seeking to build understanding rather than escalate conflict, even when facing criticism.
reflection.zh: 这篇关于“激烈冲突”的报道提醒我们言语在公共生活中的强大影响力。箴言12:18告诫我们，“言语轻率的，如刀刺人”，能够造成深刻的伤害。愿我们在言语上追求智慧，即使面对批评，也努力促进理解而非升级冲突。

verse.textEn: The words of the reckless pierce like swords, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
verse.textZh: 说话浮躁的，如刀刺人；智慧人的舌头却为医人的良药。

title.en: Indian activist on hunger strike for 20 days forcibly taken to hospital
title.zh: 印度活动家绝食20天后被强制送医

summary.en: An Indian activist, Sonam Wangchuk, was forcibly hospitalized after a 20-day hunger strike. He had been urging people to join a protest march to parliament scheduled for July 20.
summary.zh: 印度活动家索南·旺楚克在绝食20天后被强制送往医院。他此前曾呼吁民众参加定于7月20日举行的议会抗议游行。

body.en:
Indian activist and educationist Sonam Wangchuk, on hunger strike for the past 20 days in Delhi, has been forcibly removed from his protest site.

The 59-year-old had been protesting in support of an online satirical movement called the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) who are seeking educational reforms. The protesters had planned a march to India's parliament on Monday.

Wangchuk was sitting on hunger strike in the scorching summer, consuming nothing but salt and water. He had lost more than 9kg and was in a lot of pain.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has now begun an indefinite fast in his place. He says the march to parliament will go on and has called for Prime Minister Narendra Modi to resign.

Dipke told the BBC he had gone to a friend's house in the morning to freshen up when policemen turned up and refused to let him leave.

Videos from the protest site on Saturday showed chaos erupting just before 07:30 local time (02:00 GMT) when dozens of police and paramilitary personnel swooped in on the stage where the activist was lying down. Protesters who tried to stop them were pushed away.

They covered him with curtains of bedsheets before removing him from the stage. Minutes later, an ambulance was seen speeding away.

The activist's wife Gitanjali Angmo later posted on X that she was "at Safdarjung hospital where he has been admitted".

"Nothing should be administered to him orally or intravenous[ly] without taking consent from me, his family and his doctors who have been monitoring his health for the past 20 days," she wrote , external .

Dr Charu Bamba, Medical Superintendent of Safdarjung Hospital, later told news agency ANI that Wangchuk was "fully alert and stable".

"He is somewhat weak due to prolonged fasting and is experiencing mild dehydration; otherwise, all his vital parameters are stable. He is being continuously examined and monitored, and his treatment is under way," she said.

A top police official told reporters that Wangchuk had been moved "in compliance with [a court] order, and based on health conditions and medical advice".

"Sonam Wangchuk has been moved to a government hospital for much-needed medical intervention and is currently under medical supervision," said Sachin Sharma, Deputy Commissioner of Police.

He was referring to a Delhi High Court order from Thursday asking the federal government to monitor Wangchuk's health regularly and provide necessary treatment if needed.

Wangchuk had refused to end his indefinite hunger strike despite growing calls for him to do so. Despite his frail health, he had been insisting that he would participate in Monday's march to the parliament.

body.zh: 印度活动家兼教育家索南·旺楚克 (Sonam Wangchuk) 在德里绝食抗议 20 天，现已被强行带离抗议地点。 这位 59 岁的老人一直在抗议支持一个名为“蟑螂简塔党”(CJP) 的在线讽刺运动，该运动正在寻求教育改革。抗议者原计划周一向印度议会游行。 CJP 创始人阿比吉特·迪普克 (Abhijeet Dipke) 告诉 BBC，他早上去朋友家梳洗，警察出现并拒绝让他离开。 旺楚克在炎热的夏天绝食，只吃盐和水。他体重减轻了9公斤多，并且感到非常痛苦。 周六抗议现场的视频显示，当地时间 07:30（格林威治标准时间 02:00）之前爆发了混乱，数十名警察和准军事人员突然冲进了这位活动人士躺着的舞台。试图阻止他们的抗议者被推开。 他们用床单遮住了他，然后把他带下了舞台。几分钟后，一辆救护车疾驰而去。 迪普克在整个抗议活动中一直站在旺楚克身边，他说他没有被告知旺楚克被带到哪里。 一名高级警官告诉记者，旺楚克的转移是“根据[法院]命令，并基于健康状况和医疗建议”。 警察副局长萨钦·夏尔马 (Sachin Sharma) 表示：“索南·旺楚克已被转移到一家政府医院接受急需的医疗干预，目前正在接受医疗监督。” 他指的是德里高等法院周四发布的一项命令，要求联邦政府定期监测旺楚克的健康状况，并在需要时提供必要的治疗。 旺楚克拒绝结束无限期绝食，尽管要求他这样做的呼声越来越高。尽管健康状况不佳，他仍坚持参加周一前往议会的游行。 几天前，旺楚克对聚集在抗议地点简塔·曼塔天文台的人群说：“我的外表变得虚弱，但我的内心却很坚强。”他的发言赢得了欢呼和掌声。 他说：“我们将一起和平游行到议会，并在民主的祭坛前提出我们的请愿书。” 这位活动人士随后开玩笑说，如果他在游行前去世，他的“鬼魂就会加入游行”。 目前尚不清楚人民党是否仍会尝试游行到议会，但这位活动人士不太可能参加。 CJP 于 5 月开始，是一场在线讽刺运动，旨在抗议印度最高考试中的试卷泄露和其他违规行为，并在社交媒体上获得了大量追随者。 这些自称蟑螂的抗议者已经抗议一个月了。一些学生的成员...

reflection.en: An activist's hunger strike and call for protest highlight the deep human longing for justice to prevail. The prophet Amos reminds us that Yahweh desires justice to flow powerfully and consistently, like an unfailing stream. This story prompts us to consider how we, too, can contribute to a world where righteousness is evident and accessible to all.
reflection.zh: 一位活动家的绝食抗议和呼吁示威，凸显了人类对公义得以伸张的深切渴望。先知阿摩司提醒我们，雅伟渴望公义像江河般涌流，正直像永不干涸的溪流。这个故事促使我们思考，我们如何也能为一个公义彰显、人人可及的世界做出贡献。

verse.textEn: Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!
verse.textZh: 惟愿公平如大水滚滚，使公义如江河滔滔。

title.en: Control, threats, disfiguring surgery: My life inside Jeffrey Epstein's 'cult'
title.zh: 控制、威胁、毁容手术：我在杰弗里·爱泼斯坦“邪教”中的生活

summary.en: "Anya" gives the BBC a rare account of how sex-criminal financier Epstein lured and abused his “assistants”.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In the week after the sex-criminal financier Jeffrey Epstein died, Anya (not her real name) opened the door of her New York apartment. Outside was Epstein's brother, Mark, telling her she had to leave, she says.

Anya had lived for years in one of several flats on East 66th Street in Manhattan used by Jeffrey Epstein to house women he abused. In one moment, she lost her home but escaped a nightmare. (Mark Epstein denies he was aware of his brother's wrongdoing.)

"I'm still struggling to reconcile with the fact that I was abused for years," Anya says. "You were not chained to a door or something, right? You were not locked up in a basement. The chains were less obvious, but they were there."

Epstein, who died in 2019 while awaiting charges for sex-trafficking children, used to say that his operation was "like a cult, and he was the cult leader", Anya says.

She has given the BBC a rare account of life as one of Epstein's "assistants", detailing how the financier maintained a hold over so many of his victims for so long.

The assistants were a group of women - roughly a dozen at one time, Anya estimates - who were housed by Epstein, worked all hours at his beck and call, and were regularly sexually abused by him.

Anya says they were drawn in with elaborate deceptions and empty promises of work, before he began to coercively control nearly every aspect of their lives, exploiting any weaknesses he could uncover.

She says he controlled their finances, dictated who they saw and psychologically demeaned them. He monitored their bodies obsessively, Anya says, and forced her to have unnecessary, disfiguring surgery.

Her account of Epstein's control is echoed by Sarah Kellen, another former assistant. She told the US House Oversight Committee earlier this year how Epstein presented himself as the assistants' saviour. "He was very good at just decimating your ability to make your own decisions and have your own autonomy. And it made you more and more dependent on him," she said.

There is a bias which tends to make people think that only children are susceptible to this type of coercion, but "you can be groomed as an adult", says Dr Tara Quinn-Cirillo, a clinical psychologist who has worked with victims of coercive control. "You can be vulnerable to this," she says.

After Jeffrey Epstein was convicted in 2008 of abusing a teenage girl - whom he lured to his homes with the offer of work as a masseuse - he changed tactics. He began largely targeting adult women, mostly from Russia or other parts of eastern Europe.

Anya says she and many of the other women recruited still looked like teenagers, however, and she showed the BBC photos of herself at the time to demonstrate.

Anya had grown up in a Russia emerging from communist rule, with strict parents who...
body.zh: 性犯罪金融家杰弗里·爱泼斯坦去世后一周，安雅（化名）打开了她纽约公寓的门。她说，外面是爱泼斯坦的兄弟马克，告诉她必须离开。 安雅多年来一直住在曼哈顿东 66 街的几套公寓之一，杰弗里·爱泼斯坦曾用这些公寓来安置他虐待的妇女。一瞬间，她失去了家，但却逃脱了一场噩梦。 （马克·爱泼斯坦否认他知道他兄弟的不当行为。） “我仍然难以接受自己多年来遭受虐待的事实，”安雅说。 “你没有被锁在门或其他东西上，对吧？你没有被锁在地下室里。锁链不太明显，但它们就在那里。” 安雅说，爱泼斯坦于 2019 年在等待对儿童性交易的指控期间去世，他曾说他的行动“就像一个邪教，而他就是邪教领袖”。 她向英国广播公司罕见地讲述了作为爱泼斯坦的“助手”之一的生活，详细描述了这位金融家如何长期控制如此多的受害者。 这些助理是一群女性——安雅估计，一次大约有十几个——她们被爱泼斯坦安置，全天候听从他的吩咐，并经常受到他的性虐待。 安雅说，在他开始利用他能发现的任何弱点，强制控制他们生活的几乎各个方面之前，他们被精心设计的欺骗和空洞的工作承诺所吸引。 她说他控制了他们的财务，决定了他们会见谁，并在心理上贬低了他们。安雅说，他痴迷地监视着他们的身体，并强迫她进行不必要的毁容手术。 她对爱泼斯坦控制权的描述得到了另一位前助理莎拉·凯伦的呼应。今年早些时候，她告诉美国众议院监督委员会，爱泼斯坦如何将自己描绘成助手们的救世主。 “他非常擅长削弱你自己做决定和拥有自主权的能力。这让你越来越依赖他，”她说。 曾与强制控制受害者合作的临床心理学家塔拉·奎因-西里洛博士表示，存在一种偏见，往往使人们认为只有孩子才容易受到这种类型的强制，但“你可以像成年人一样被培养”。 “你可能很容易受到这种影响，”她说。 2008 年，杰弗里·爱泼斯坦 (Jeffrey Epstein) 因虐待一名少女而被定罪后，他以按摩师的工作将女孩引诱到自己家中，之后他改变了策略。他开始主要针对成年女性，其中大部分来自俄罗斯或东欧其他地区。 安雅说，她和其他许多被招募的女性看起来仍然像青少年，她还展示了自己当时在 BBC 上的照片来展示。 安雅在摆脱共产主义统治的俄罗斯长大，父母严厉……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: ‘It’s only going to get worse’: wildfires forcing firefighters to make impossible choices
title.zh: “情况只会变得更糟”：野火迫使消防员做出不可能的选择

summary.en: As the climate crisis fuels more intense blazes, pushing them to new parts of the world, those tackling them are forced to ration resources and decide which to fight César Alcaraz had only just become a firefighter in the late 1990s when he found himself ambushed by a...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: As the climate crisis fuels more intense blazes, pushing them to new parts of the world, those tackling them are forced to ration resources and decide which to fight César Alcaraz had only just become a firefighter in the late 1990s when he found himself ambushed by a fast-moving blaze. Barely able to breathe and with no more water left in his truck, he and his colleagues fled an inferno ravaging Spain’s Montgó mountain region, wishing their bosses had sent more support. But nearly three decades on, as an officer with Alicante’s provincial firefighters, Alcaraz has more sympathy for the agonising choices that commanders have to make. When wildfires overwhelm an area, his job resembles that of a doctor in an emergency room with too few ventilators. Continue reading...
body.zh: 随着气候危机引发更猛烈的火灾，将火势推向世界新的地区，应对这些问题的人们被迫配给资源并决定扑灭哪些火势。塞萨尔·阿尔卡拉斯 (César Alcaraz) 在 20 世纪 90 年代末才刚刚成为一名消防员，就发现自己遭到了一场快速蔓延的大火的伏击。他和同事们几乎无法呼吸，卡车里也没有水了，他们逃离了肆虐西班牙蒙戈山区的大火，希望他们的老板能提供更多支持。但近三十年后，作为阿利坎特省消防队员的一名警官，阿尔卡拉兹对指挥官必须做出的痛苦选择更加同情。当野火淹没一个地区时，他的工作就像是呼吸机太少的急诊室里的医生。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to stewardship, provision, and the common good. 1 Peter 4:10 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with stewardship that serves neighbours, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到管家责任、供应与公共福祉。1 Peter 4:10提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以服事邻舍的好管家心态来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: US strikes hit Iran for seventh consecutive night
title.zh: 美国连续第七晚袭击伊朗

summary.en: The US military has conducted further strikes against Iran for the seventh consecutive night, aiming to degrade its armed forces, while Iran has reported explosions near the Strait of Hormuz.
summary.zh: 美国军方连续第七晚对伊朗发动袭击，旨在削弱其武装力量，与此同时，伊朗报告霍尔木兹海峡附近发生爆炸。

body.en:
The US military said it carried out the seventh night of strikes on Iran since President Donald Trump declared the temporary ceasefire agreement was "over".

In a statement shared on X, US Central Command (Centcom) wrote that its forces "hit surveillance sites, military logistics infrastructure, underground weapons storage, and maritime capabilities".

Iran claimed to have responded by targeting US allies in the region, including Kuwait – whose army said its air defences had been "confronting hostile missile and drone attacks" following "Iranian aggression".

Jordan's military also said it had intercepted 10 Iranian missiles fired into its airspace overnight. No damage was reported.

Centcom said it had ended its strikes at 21:30 ET (02:30 BST) after several hours.

"U.S. forces employed fighter aircraft, aerial drones, and warships in addition to other assets," it said in its statement.

Iran's state-run Fars agency had said two oil tankers "exploded and caught fire while passing through a mined route south of the Strait of Hormuz". Later, Centcom posted on X: "Like most IRGC claims, this is false."

Shipping traffic in the vital Strait of Hormuz has largely stopped amid the continuing tit-for-tat strikes by US and Iranian forces. The strait normally accounts for about one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supplies.

Explosions were heard in the central city of Yazd and at Qeshm island and the port of Bandar Abbas next to the strait, Iranian state media reported.

On Friday, Iran's armed forces claimed to have attacked multiple US military facilities across the Gulf region in Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan and – for the first time – Syria, which the US denied.

Earlier, Kuwaiti officials said Iranian drone strikes had injured a number of their soldiers, while a power plant and water desalination stations had also been damaged.

Sources have told the BBC's US partner CBS news that several American service members were injured during Iranian attacks on two Jordanian bases over the past week.

Washington denied Tehran's earlier claims that its forces hit civilian infrastructure in Iran, including bridges, a train station and an airport. Provincial authorities in the affected region, Hormozgan province, said seven people were killed in the attacks.

BBC Verify and BBC Persian have verified footage of damage to Gariveh Bridge, after night videos showed a ball of flames on top of it.

Daylight images showed a crumbled stretch of road with rubble around the broken bridge.

A White House spokesperson told the BBC the US had "carried out strikes exclusively on military targets, including military logistics infrastructure".

Friday marked one week of nightly US attacks since peace talks with Iran collapsed, as tensions over the future of the Strait...
body.zh: 美国军方表示，自美国总统唐纳德·特朗普宣布临时停火协议“结束”以来，这是对伊朗进行的第七晚袭击。 美军中央司令部（Centcom）在一份声明中表示：“这些袭击的目的是在总司令的指示下继续削弱伊朗的军事能力。” 伊朗革命卫队（IRGC）表示，两艘油轮在霍尔木兹海峡经过航道布雷区时发生爆炸，中央司令部后来驳回这一说法，认为这是虚假的。 伊朗媒体报道称，中部城市亚兹德、格什姆岛以及海峡附近的阿巴斯港均听到爆炸声。 伊朗国营法尔斯机构表示，两艘油轮“在经过霍尔木兹海峡以南的一条布有布雷的路线时爆炸并起火”。 由于美国和伊朗军队持续针锋相对的打击，重要的霍尔木兹海峡的航运交通已基本停止。正常情况下，该海峡约占世界石油和液化天然气供应量的五分之一。 周五，伊朗武装部队声称袭击了海湾地区科威特、巴林、约旦和叙利亚的多个美国军事设施，但美国否认了这一说法。 早些时候，科威特官员表示，伊朗无人机袭击造成多名科威特士兵受伤，一座发电厂和海水淡化站也遭到损坏。 消息人士告诉英国广播公司的美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，过去一周伊朗袭击约旦两个基地时，数名美国军人受伤。 华盛顿否认德黑兰早些时候声称其部队袭击了伊朗的民用基础设施，包括桥梁、火车站和机场。霍尔木兹甘省受影响地区的省级当局表示，袭击造成七人死亡。 BBC verify 和 BBC Persian 已经核实了加里维桥受损的镜头，夜间视频显示桥顶有一团火球。 日光图像显示断桥周围有一段破碎的道路，断桥周围有瓦砾。 白宫发言人告诉英国广播公司，美国“专门针对军事目标进行了打击，包括军事后勤基础设施”。 自与伊朗和谈破裂以来，周五是美国每晚发动袭击的一周，霍尔木兹海峡未来的紧张局势阻碍了促成永久停火的努力。

reflection.en: The ongoing cycle of military strikes and reported explosions highlights the perilous nature of escalating conflict. Yahweh's word reminds us that violence often begets more violence, trapping all involved in a dangerous spiral. May leaders seek paths that break this cycle, rather than perpetuate it.
reflection.zh: 军事打击和爆炸报告的持续循环，凸显了冲突升级的危险性。雅伟的话语提醒我们，暴力往往滋生更多的暴力，使所有卷入其中的人陷入危险的漩涡。愿领袖们寻求打破而非延续这一循环的道路。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

title.en: ‘We are preserving a tradition’: how Ghana’s sensationalist film posters became collectible art
title.zh: “我们正在传承一种传统”：加纳耸人听闻的电影海报如何成为收藏艺术品

summary.en: Hand-painted film posters from Ghana, known for their sensational and often unfaithful reinterpretations of movies, have become sought-after collectible art. However, their misleading nature sometimes provoked strong negative reactions, including threats and physical attacks, from viewers who felt deceived.
summary.zh: 加纳手绘电影海报因其夸张且常与电影内容不符的重新诠释而闻名，现已成为备受追捧的收藏艺术品。然而，这些具有误导性的海报有时会激起观众强烈的负面反应，包括来自感到受骗的观众的威胁和人身攻击。

body.en: Hand-painted works are often wildly unfaithful to the movies they portray – reinterpretations that sometimes resulted in threats, insults and even physical attacks from viewers who felt duped Sitting on his porch in Teshie near Accra, Heavy J dipped a brush into red oil paint and dabbed it carefully on to his canvas – a flour sack – adding blood to a knife being wielded by a man. Higher on the canvas, he had started on an outline of a skull. Heavy J was creating a poster, but not as you might have expected for a horror film. Instead, it was for the animated fairytale The Little Mermaid. The man with the knife wasn’t a killer but the film’s kind-hearted prince, Eric. The skull was also unrelated to the story. “We add more to make people interested,” said Heavy J, whose real name is Jeaurs Affutu. Continue reading...
body.zh: 手绘作品往往对他们所描绘的电影非常不忠实——重新解释有时会导致观众的威胁、侮辱，甚至人身攻击，他们觉得自己被骗了。Heavy J 坐在阿克拉附近特西的门廊上，用画笔蘸上红色油画，小心地涂抹在他的画布——一个面粉袋上——为一名男子挥舞的一把刀增添了血迹。在画布的更高处，他开始画出头骨的轮廓。 Heavy J 正在制作一张海报，但并不像你想象的那样是一部恐怖电影。相反，它是为了动画童话《小美人鱼》。持刀男子并不是杀手，而是影片中善良的王子埃里克。头骨也与故事无关。 “我们添加更多内容是为了让人们感兴趣，”Heavy J 说，他的真名是 Jeaurs Affutu。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The vibrant Ghanaian film posters, while now celebrated as art, highlight the tension between creative expression and honest representation. When communication, even artistic, is "wildly unfaithful" to reality, it can lead to feelings of deception and strong negative reactions from those who feel misled. Yahweh calls us to put away falsehood and speak...
reflection.zh: 这些充满活力的加纳电影海报，如今虽被誉为艺术品，却也凸显了创意表达与真实呈现之间的张力。当沟通，即使是艺术形式的沟通，与现实“严重不符”时，可能导致感到受骗的人产生被欺骗感和强烈的负面反应。雅伟呼召我们弃绝谎言，说出真理，认识到我们的言语和图像对邻舍有着真实的影响。

verse.textEn: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to your neighbor.

title.en: 'They’re at it again': The Australian caught in the enduring dispute over the Falklands
title.zh: “他们又来了”：《澳大利亚人报》陷入了关于福克兰群岛的持久争端

summary.en: Australian Sally Poncet has lived in the remote island community for more than 40 years.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Another clash in one of football's fiercest rivalries has sent shockwaves through the island community that Tasmanian-born Sally Poncet calls home.

After a come-from-behind triumph over their English adversaries in the semi-finals of the FIFA World Cup on Thursday , Argentinian players unfurled a banner on the pitch in Atlanta reiterating their national claim over the islands less than 500km from their coastline.

"Los Malvinas Son Argentinas" (The Falklands are Argentine), the controversial banner read, using the Argentinian name for the South Atlantic islands that have been occupied by Britain since 1833.

For Poncet, who first fell in love with the place after seeing it from her yacht sailed with her then-husband in 1979, the move was a "crass" and "ignorant" display, but one she is more than accustomed to.

"It's just part of what we have to deal with," she told SBS News over the phone from the capital, Stanley. "It's just having a bully for a neighbour."

Poncet settled on the Falklands in 1983, exactly one year after the end of the war over the territory between Argentina and Britain that killed 649 and 255 people from each country, respectively.

The shadow of that 74-day conflict, which began when the ruling Argentine military junta launched a surprise invasion and occupation, has never gone away, she said.

"It was huge, and it still is," she added. "We still live under threat and that history that we didn't ask for. We don't want it again, obviously, but we're still having to live with it."

Just 3,600 people live on the islands that are roughly comparable in size to the greater Sydney metropolitan area.

While it has an independent government, it relies entirely on the United Kingdom for geopolitical matters.

Outgoing UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer supported calls made to FIFA by UK business minister Peter Kyle, who has demanded an investigation into the banner-waving incident.

Kyle called the flag waving an "egregious violation" of FIFA rules, which ban political symbols on the field of play.

"The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are," a Downing Street spokesperson said.

FIFA has said it is "assessing match reports" under "standard procedure", but it is not clear whether an investigation has been launched.

Right-wing Argentine President Javier Milei described the players' move as "perfectly valid and legitimate".

"The Malvinas are Argentine, we're going to recover them, and we will do it through diplomatic means."

The islands, which were previously uninhabited, were discovered by a British captain in 1690.

title.en: Brad Pitt's children are dropping their dad's surname - here's why I did the same
title.zh: 布拉德·皮特的子女放弃父亲的姓氏——这就是我这样做的原因

summary.en: A news story highlights how children of celebrity Brad Pitt are reportedly dropping their father's surname, drawing parallels with another individual's personal decision to legally change her name after years of using her mother's maiden name on social media.
summary.zh: 一则新闻报道指出，名人格拉德·皮特的子女据称正在放弃他们父亲的姓氏，并将其与另一位个人在社交媒体上使用母亲的娘家姓多年后，合法更改姓氏的个人决定进行比较。

body.en:
On social media, sports rosters, email and restaurant bookings, she was Hannah Leonard, sharing her surname with her mother.

But legally, and at work and school, she had a different surname - the one she inherited from her father.

Hannah's parents divorced when she was a toddler and she hasn't had much of a relationship with her dad since. She says she last saw him seven years ago and isn't sure where he's living now.

Last month, the 25-year-old in California legally changed her surname to Leonard-Ripley, removing the reminder of her father and replacing it with a name combining her mother's maiden name and her husband's surname.

That same month, two of the adopted children of Hollywood divorcees Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt undertook an important legal step in the process to drop their father's surname, something they began earlier this year.

In April, Zahara Marley Jolie-Pitt and Maddox Chivan Jolie-Pitt, aged 21 and 24, filed documents to remove their father's surname from their names, according to media reports.

In June and July, the siblings carried out the legal requirement of publishing their name-change intention in a local paper for four weeks.

Both have already used the surname Jolie in some circumstances, including Zahara during her graduation ceremony earlier this year and Maddox in his credits on a film. Another of Jolie and Pitt's six children, Shiloh, changed her surname to Jolie in 2024.

Zahara and Maddox will have to wait until their court appearances in September to get the approval from a judge to change their names.

Jolie met Pitt on the set of the 2005 film Mr and Mrs Smith, married in 2014 and filed for divorce in 2016 following an incident on board a private plane. Jolie told Vogue , external in 2020 that she had left Pitt for the "wellbeing" of her family.

A source close to Pitt told BBC News that he regretted how things had unfolded with his family and that, while he was "heartbroken", he respected his children's decisions.

Hannah says she had no emotional connection to her previous surname, and it often confused people when she would use two surnames in different contexts.

She had wanted to legally change her surname for years, but had been deterred by the cost. Getting married gave her the push to finally make the change.

"I've never felt like my last name reflected the love that encompasses my life," Hannah says. "And I wanted to make sure that my name reflected that. My mother's love and also my husband's love are very abundant and so important to me."

"Surnames have a close connection to identity," says University of Chester lecturer Dr Harry Parkin, who has studied the history of names. When people change theirs, it can be a sign that they want to disconnect and disassociate from it, he adds.

title.zh: 特朗普指责加拿大对美国造成山火烟雾并要求赔偿

summary.en: The US president has complained that the country is being "invaded by filthy air" while the Canadian PM asks for assistance.

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has attacked Canada for wildfire smoke spreading across the United States and said he would add the "incalculable cost" of dealing with the pollution to existing tariffs on Canadian goods.

Heavy smoke from hundreds of Canadian fires enveloped large parts of the US, from the Midwest to the Northeast, this week, prompting warnings to residents to stay indoors.

Trump, who has a combative relationship with Prime Minister Mark Carney, said he would be calling the Canadian leader to find out what he planned to do about the "totally unacceptable" situation.

"We are holding Canada responsible for the fact that they are not properly maintaining their Forests ... and the United States is being unnecessarily invaded by filthy, polluted, and unhealthy air," he said in a Truth Social post.

"This is Willful Negligence, and becoming a yearly occurrence, costing the United States Billions of Dollars, which cost of this pollution must of necessity be added to the TARIFFS Canada is currently paying."

Climate experts, however, say higher temperatures have led to drier forests and more wildfires in recent years. Canada has one of the world's largest forests.

"As our climate warms, we're seeing more conducive hot, dry, windy, more extreme weather, and we're going to see more fire," said Mike Flannigan, a professor of wildland fire at Thompson Rivers University in British Columbia.

Shortly after taking office in 2025, Trump imposed tariffs on several key imports from Canada.

Carney said on Thursday the United States could do more to combat climate change that is leading to warmer and more extreme temperatures around the world.

The two men are likely to meet at the FIFA World Cup final in New Jersey on Monday.

Many blazes this year are in the giant province of Ontario and are concentrated in the remote and sparsely populated northwest, where the only mode of transport is plane.

Namaygoosisagagun First Nation, also known as Collins First Nation, in northwestern Ontario was burned to the ground, forcing residents to evacuate by boat and seek shelter in Thunder Bay, Matthew Hoppe, the community's incident commander, told the Reuters news agency.

"There was nothing remaining. So as you can imagine, the membership is totally distraught, upset, overwhelmed, lost," Hoppe said.

Thunder Bay, a city of about 110,000 people on the northern shore of Lake Superior more than 1,300km northwest of Toronto, is at full capacity from sheltering wildfire evacuees from across northwestern Ontario, Mayor Ken Boshcoff said.

title.en: Iran hits US Middle East allies in retaliation for expanded US strikes
title.zh: 中东战火蔓延，美伊互袭基础设施

summary.en: Bridges, train lines, power and water facilities, and others have been struck in Iran, Kuwait, and elsewhere in the Middle East.

body.en:
Iran launched renewed attacks on United States Gulf allies on Saturday after a seventh straight night of US strikes targeting Iranian military sites, including logistics infrastructure.

Both sides also took aim at shipping traffic, with the US saying it was enforcing a naval blockade, while Iran said it targeted vessels that violated its rules on navigating the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway for one-fifth of the world's oil supply .

Oil prices climbed more than 4 per cent on Friday to their highest level in more than a month, applying political pressure on US President Donald Trump as his Republican Party tries to hold on to power in November's congressional elections.

Washington and Tehran have been testing the limits of escalation since their ceasefire agreement collapsed on 8 July, raising the prospect of a return to all-out war.

The US military's Central Command said it concluded its latest round of attacks by hitting surveillance sites, military logistics infrastructure, underground weapons storage and maritime capabilities.

"US forces employed fighter aircraft, aerial drones, and warships in addition to other assets," Central Command said in a statement. "More than 50,000 American service members are operating across the Middle East and remain vigilant, lethal, and ready."

Iranian media reported on Saturday that several missiles struck power facilities and desalination pumps in the southern Iranian city of Jask, citing a local official. The official said drinking water had been cut off in villages in Jask due to the attack.

The US said its forces redirected four commercial vessels, disabled one, and boarded another to enforce its naval blockade of Iran.

In turn, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four vessels violating its rules on shipping traffic were stopped from going through the strait with a combined missile and drone operation.

In addition, Iranian media, citing Iran's Revolutionary Guards, reported that two oil tankers exploded and caught fire after passing through a mined route south of the strait. The US military labelled that report as false.

Armed men seized another vessel off Yemen, raising concern over security in the Middle East's other big choke point for oil shipments at the mouth of the Red Sea.

Iran's state television quoted the Revolutionary Guards as saying that until US "aggression" comes to an end, it will not be possible to export chemical fertilisers or even a "single drop of oil and gas" from the region.

"Eight people were killed after Israeli warplanes struck a gathering of civilians in the Al-Balata market area of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza," reported Gaza's civil defense agency, which functions as a rescue service under Hamas .

Israel's military (IDF) said it had struck a "terrorist cell" from the Palestinian Islamic Jihad militant group and that it was aware civilians may have been harmed in the strike.

"A short while ago, the IDF struck a terrorist cell of the Islamic Jihad terrorist organisation in the central Gaza Strip," the military said.

"The IDF is aware of the claims that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strike. The results of the strike are under review."

Israel and Hamas agreed to a ceasefire deal in October aimed at halting a two-year-long war sparked by the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks on Israel.

However, according to Gaza's Health Ministry operating under Hamas authority, at least 1,127 Palestinians have been killed since the truce took effect.

The IDF says at least five soldiers have been killed in Gaza over the corresponding period.

title.en: Germany’s 5,000 heat deaths: What the numbers reveal
title.zh: 德国5000人死于高温：数字揭示了什么

summary.en: The Robert Koch Institute reported that over 5,100 people in Germany died from heat-related causes by the end of June this year, raising questions about how researchers confirm such deaths.
summary.zh: 罗伯特·科赫研究所报告称，截至今年6月底，德国有超过5100人死于与高温相关的原因，这引发了研究人员如何确认此类死亡的疑问。

body.en:
More than 5,100 people in Germany died from heat-related causes this year until the end of June, the Robert Koch Institute reports. But how can researchers prove that someone died because of soaring temperatures?

A heatstroke begins with headaches , dizziness and loss of awareness. The body’s regulation system fails, causing body temperature to rise to life-threatening levels. Multiple organ failure and death can follow. But doctors rarely record deaths that can be directly attributed to heat. According to Germany’s Federal Statistical Office, an average of 21 such cases were recorded each year between 2004 and 2014.

The 5,120 heat-related deaths in Germany in 2026 through June 28, published by the Robert Koch Institute (RKI) , is therefore an estimate. But that does not mean the figure is pulled out of thin air. "It is based on a statistical correlation," says Alexandra Schneider, a meteorologist, epidemiologist and deputy director of the Institute of Epidemiology at Helmholtz Munich.

This estimate was found by comparing death figures collected by Germany’s Federal Statistical Office with temperature trends over a given period measured by the German Weather Service. In the final week of June alone, around 23,600 people died. The weekly average temperature — meaning the average daytime and nighttime temperature over the course of a week — was 26 degrees Celsius. The RKI assumes that heat-related deaths occur from a weekly average temperature of 20 degrees Celsius onward.

The number of deaths in that final week of June was nearly 30% higher than the average for comparable periods in previous years, when around 18,200 people died. To estimate the number of heat-related deaths, researchers modeled how many deaths would have occurred under conditions with temperatures of no more than 20 degrees Celsius.

Researchers also adjust for certain confounding factors, Schneider explains. Using this method, the RKI estimates that there were 5,120 heat-related deaths — with 4,310 of those occurring in the final week of June alone.

Alexandra Schneider considers the estimate plausible and says she expected a figure of this magnitude. In the past, the epidemiologist has criticized the RKI’s methodology. "If temperatures fluctuate sharply within a week, using a weekly average can smooth out those extremes and lead to an underestimation of deaths," she explains. "This time, however, it was consistently hot."

The same applies to cold-related deaths as to heat-related deaths: they are estimates based on a plausible statistical link. During colder months, respiratory illnesses become more common. Cold temperatures also contribute to cardiovascular diseases, just as heat does, explains epidemiologist Schneider.

title.en: Why the US is going after the International Criminal Court
title.zh: 美国为何追查国际刑事法院

summary.en: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has ramped up his criticism of the International Criminal Court in The Hague. His gloves-off approach could have far-reaching consequences for the tribunal.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has ramped up his criticism of the International Criminal Court in The Hague. His gloves-off approach could have far-reaching consequences for the tribunal.

In The Hague there are two major international courts that are often confused. One is the UN's International Court of Justice (ICJ ), based in the historic Peace Palace, which settles disputes between states. The other is the International Criminal Court (ICC) , established in 2002 to prosecute individuals for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. Housed in a modern glass-and-concrete building, the ICC has 125 member states — not all 193 UN members. The US, Russia and China are among the countries that have not joined, along with several states in Asia and North Africa.

When US Secretary of State Marco Rubio recently threatened to dismantle the court "brick by brick," it was clear he was referring to the ICC. In a statement, the State Department outlined a number of measures Washington is considering as part of its campaign against the court. These include visa restrictions on ICC staff and tougher sanctions targeting the court and affiliated organizations. It also suggested increased scrutiny of countries "that refuse to reject the ICC's illegitimate authority" while continuing to receive US assistance.

The US has clashed with the ICC before . But legal experts around the world say Washington's latest escalation marks a significant shift.

"What the US and Marco Rubio have now essentially done is make public something that has been going on for more than a year. The US has been using various forms of diplomatic pressure against other countries in an effort to change their positions, and in some cases their voting behavior, toward the ICC," says Andreas Schüller, co-director of the International Crimes and Legal Accountability Program at the European Center for Constitutional and Human Rights (ECCHR) in Berlin.

"The fact that it is now being declared a campaign shows that it is being pursued strategically, that it is broader in scope, and that other countries — including those that are not ICC members — are also being brought on board to help apply pressure," Schüller told DW.

The US is not a member of the International Criminal Court, meaning crimes committed on US soil do not fall under its jurisdiction. But the ICC can prosecute alleged atrocities committed in member states — a principle that led, for example, to arrest warrants being issued for Russian President Vladimir Putin and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu .

body.zh: 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥加大了对海牙国际刑事法院的批评力度。他的不干涉行为可能会对法庭产生深远的影响。 海牙有两个经常被混淆的主要国际法院。其中之一是位于历史悠久的和平宫的联合国国际法院（ICJ），负责解决国家之间的争端。另一个是国际刑事法院（ICC），成立于2002年，负责起诉犯有战争罪、反人类罪和种族灭绝罪的个人。国际刑事法院坐落在一座现代化的玻璃和混凝土建筑内，拥有 125 个成员国——并非全部 193 个联合国成员国。美国、俄罗斯和中国以及亚洲和北非的几个国家都没有加入。 当美国国务卿马可·卢比奥最近威胁要“一砖一瓦”解散该法院时，很明显他指的是国际刑事法院。美国国务院在一份声明中概述了华盛顿正在考虑采取的一系列措施，作为其针对该法院的行动的一部分。其中包括对国际刑事法院工作人员的签证限制以及针对法院及其附属组织的更严厉制裁。它还建议加强对“拒绝拒绝国际刑事法院非法权威”同时继续接受美国援助的国家的审查。 美国此前曾与国际刑事法院发生过冲突。但世界各地的法律专家表示，华盛顿最近的升级标志着一个重大转变。 柏林欧洲宪法与人权中心 (ECCHR) 国际犯罪和法律问责项目联席主任安德烈亚斯·舒勒 (Andreas Schüller) 表示：“美国和卢比奥现在所做的实质上就是将已经发生一年多的事情公之于众。美国一直在对其他国家施加各种形式的外交压力，试图改变它们对国际刑事法院的立场，在某些情况下甚至改变它们的投票行为。” 舒勒告诉德国之声：“事实上，它现在被宣布为一场运动，这表明它是在战略上进行的，范围更广泛，其他国家——包括非国际刑事法院成员国——也被拉拢进来，帮助施加压力。” 美国不是国际刑事法院的成员，这意味着在美国境内犯下的罪行不属于其管辖范围。但国际刑事法院可以起诉在成员国犯下的暴行——这一原则导致对俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡发出逮捕令。 国际刑事法院的根源在于历史的教训。二战后的纽伦堡审判对纳粹头目进行了审判，标志着现代国际刑法的诞生。战争罪行之后...

title.en: Why Pauline Hanson's appearance on Tommy Robinson's podcast is so controversial

summary.en: Pauline Hanson's appearance on a podcast with a far-right UK activist has drawn significant public criticism, though it also received a defense from Barnaby Joyce.

body.en:
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has drawn criticism for appearing on a podcast with controversial far-right UK activist Tommy Robinson, where she pointed to the scrapping of the White Australia policy as the root cause of migration issues in the country.

The nearly hour-long conversation, recorded last week during Hanson's visit to the UK, was published on Robinson's podcast on Friday.

The appearance has since drawn criticism from other politicians, though not everyone in Canberra has condemned it.

Between speaking about her scepticism about the COVID-19 vaccine, the potential for her daughter to eventually lead One Nation, and reflections on her time in prison and her burqa incidents in parliament , Hanson focused heavily on immigration.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Asked by Robinson how Australia had ended up with "Pakistanis, Somalis, all of these African problems with violent Africans," Hanson said it started with the end of the White Australia Policy.

The postwar wave of migrants was different to today's situation because the new arrivals "really assimilated' and "learned to speak English", she said.

Hanson also suggested migrants were often coming to Australia "purely for the welfare system", claiming Australian Muslims were having children because the Quran taught "Allah will provide".

She said people were coming to Australia to take advantage of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), saying people from "Muslim areas" were "ripping the system off".

She said "a lot" of the scheme's nearly 800,000 participants came from those communities, but offered no evidence for the claim.

"But there’s a lot of Aussies too," she added. "So I’m not just going to pick them out, but it is quite known that in the Muslim streets you’ve got quite a lot in that street who are on the NDIS scheme."

Hanson has previously called for a " monocultural " society, saying multiculturalism in Australia has "failed".

During her first National Press Club address in June , she targeted the one in four Australians who speak other languages at home, saying it was impossible to generate social cohesion if people can't speak English.

Health and NDIS Minister Mark Butler said he was loath to respond to the podcast because Robinson was a convicted criminal who'd been disowned by leading figures on the right, but added he'd never seen a breakdown in nationality or religious background of NDIS participants.

"I'm not sure where Ms Hanson is getting her figures from, but they've never been provided to me ... I suspect they don't exist," he told ABC Radio National on Friday.

body.zh: 一国党领导人宝琳·汉森因与有争议的英国极右翼活动人士汤米·罗宾逊一起出现在播客中而受到批评，她在播客中指出废除白澳政策是该国移民问题的根本原因。 这段近一个小时的谈话是汉森上周访问英国期间录制的，周五在罗宾逊的播客上发布。 此后，这次露面引起了其他政客的批评，但并非堪培拉的每个人都谴责这一行为。 在谈到她对 COVID-19 疫苗的怀疑、她女儿最终领导一国党的潜力，以及对她在监狱中的经历和议会中的罩袍事件的反思时，汉森重点关注了移民问题。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 当罗宾逊问澳大利亚如何结束“巴基斯坦人、索马里人以及所有这些非洲人与暴力非洲人之间的问题”时，汉森说，这始于白澳大利亚政策的结束。 她说，战后的移民浪潮与今天的情况不同，因为新来者“真正被同化”并“学会了说英语”。 汉森还表示，移民经常“纯粹为了福利制度”来到澳大利亚，并声称澳大利亚穆斯林之所以生孩子，是因为《古兰经》教导“安拉会提供”。 她说，人们来到澳大利亚是为了利用国家伤残保险计划（NDIS），并称来自“穆斯林地区”的人们正在“窃取该系统”。 她说，该计划的近 80 万名参与者中“很多”来自这些社区，但没有提供证据证明这一说法。 “但也有很多澳大利亚人，”她补充道。 “所以我不仅仅要把他们挑出来，而且众所周知，在穆斯林街道上，有很多人都参加了 NDIS 计划。” 汉森此前曾呼吁建立一个“单一文化”社会，称澳大利亚的多元文化主义已经“失败”。 在六月的第一次全国新闻俱乐部演讲中，她针对四分之一在家里说其他语言的澳大利亚人，表示如果人们不会说英语，就不可能产生社会凝聚力。 卫生部和 NDIS 部长马克·巴特勒 (Mark Butler) 表示，他不愿对播客做出回应，因为罗宾逊是一名已被定罪的罪犯，已被右翼领导人断绝关系，但他补充说，他从未见过 NDIS 参与者的国籍或宗教背景细分。 “我不确定汉森女士从哪里得到她的数据，但它们从未提供给我......我怀疑它们不存在，”他周五告诉美国广播公司国家广播电台。 巴特勒说汉森需要解释她为什么要去......

title.en: China hits out at British Steel nationalisation
title.zh: 中国抨击英国钢铁国有化

summary.en: The UK government announced the nationalization of British Steel, stating the move was to protect a crucial national capability. China subsequently expressed strong disapproval of this decision.
summary.zh: 英国政府宣布将英国钢铁公司收归国有，称此举旨在维护“一项重要的国家能力”。中国随后对此决定表示强烈不满。

body.en:
China has hit out at the nationalisation of British Steel, saying it "firmly opposes and is strongly dissatisfied with the British government's decision".

On Thursday, the UK government said that taking the loss-making firm into public hands would protect jobs and safeguard a "vital national capability".

The UK took control of British Steel's operations in Scunthorpe last year, though it was still owned by China's Jingye Group, limiting the government's ability to steer its future.

China's commerce ministry said on Friday that the moves "seriously infringed upon Jingye's legitimate rights and interests and severely undermined the confidence of Chinese companies investing in the UK".

It also called on Britain to "faithfully fulfil" its obligations under the China–UK Bilateral Investment Treaty.

"Disregarding Jingye's significant contribution to the UK economy and society, the British side forcibly took control of the company in the name of national security," the ministry said.

The statement added that Beijing would monitor developments closely and support Chinese firms to protect their rights, but did not specify what protecting Chinese companies' rights might involve.

The decision to nationalise British Steel threatens to strain the relationship between London and Beijing just as Andy Burnham is set to enter Downing Street on Monday.

The incoming prime minister will have to weigh his approach to the issue with the economic benefits of ties with the world's second largest economy.

The China-UK Bilateral Investment Treaty is a legally binding agreement that was signed in 1986. It was designed to promote and protect investments between the two countries.

On Friday, a UK government spokesperson said it had held negotiations with Jingye but it "wasn't possible to reach an agreement that represented value to the taxpayer".

"We highly value our relationship with China and remain open to Chinese investment," the spokesperson added.

The nationalisation came after Parliament on Wednesday passed legislation allowing the government to bring the steel industry into public ownership under circumstances where it met a public interest test.

Jingye is seeking compensation, having previously said the business was losing £700,000 a day. The BBC has been unable to get a response from Jingye itself to Thursday's announcement.

Small Business Minister Blair McDougall told the House of Commons on Thursday that the government will appoint an independent valuer in the autumn "to make a judgment on any compensation that is due, and that could be nil".

By taking British Steel into public ownership the government now has the power and freedom to decide on the future of the plant, while keeping the blast furnaces going.

body.zh: 中方对英国钢铁公司国有化予以猛烈抨击，称“坚决反对，对英国政府的决定表示强烈不满”。 周四，英国政府表示，将这家亏损公司纳入公众手中将保护就业并维护“重要的国家能力”。 英国去年控制了英国钢铁公司在斯肯索普的业务，尽管该公司仍由中国敬业集团所有，这限制了政府掌控其未来的能力。 中国商务部周五表示，此举“严重侵犯敬业公司的合法权益，严重损害中国企业对英国投资的信心”。 它还呼吁英国“忠实履行”中英双边投资条约规定的义务。 英方无视敬业公司对英国经济社会的重大贡献，以国家安全为名，强行控制敬业公司。 声明补充说，北京将密切关注事态发展并支持中国企业保护自身权利，但没有具体说明保护中国企业权利可能涉及哪些内容。 就在安迪·伯纳姆将于周一就任英国首相之际，英国钢铁公司国有化的决定可能会导致伦敦和北京之间的关系紧张。 即将上任的总理必须权衡自己处理这一问题的方法与与世界第二大经济体建立联系的经济利益。 《中英双边投资条约》是1986年签署的具有法律约束力的协议，旨在促进和保护两国之间的投资。 周三，议会通过了一项立法，允许政府在满足公共利益要求的情况下将钢铁行业纳入公有制。 敬业正在寻求赔偿，此前曾表示该业务每天损失 70 万英镑。 BBC 尚未得到敬业本身对周四的公告的回应。 通过将英国钢铁公司纳入公有制，政府现在拥有决定工厂未来的权力和自由，同时保持高炉的运转。 从长远来看，政府不太可能继续经营该业务，因为每天的成本超过一百万英镑。 3 月份，国家审计办公室表示，斯肯索普钢铁厂每天给政府造成的损失约为 130 万英镑。 商务大臣彼得·凯尔告诉英国广播公司，政府需要“在不久的将来”承担运营成本。

verse.textEn: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms.
verse.textZh: 因我们并不是与属血气的争战，乃是与那些执政的、掌权的、管辖这幽暗世界的，以及天空属灵气的恶魔争战。

title.en: Beijing’s message to the world’s tourists: come here and judge China for yourselves | Zichen Wang
title.zh: 北京向世界游客发出信息：来中国，亲自评判

summary.en: Beijing has relaxed its visa rules, aiming to boost its economy and enhance its international image. The move has led to a noticeable return of foreign tourists to the capital, engaging in sightseeing and local activities.
summary.zh: 北京放宽了签证规定，旨在提振经济并改善其国际形象。此举已使外国游客明显回流首都，他们正在观光并参与当地活动。

body.en: By relaxing visa rules, Beijing has two things on its mind – boosting its economy and improving its self-image Walk through central Beijing today and one thing quickly becomes apparent: foreigners are back. They are taking photos outside the Forbidden City and sitting in cafes around Gulou and Sanlitun. The shift is visible online, too; YouTube is increasingly filled with videos titled “China Shocked Me” or “My First Week in China”. Most of the creators are tourists, not China specialists or journalists, and many of them are encountering the country for the first time. The resurgence is striking because to many outside observers China’s story has become one of closure and increased security – of intensifying strategic rivalry with the west, expanded anti-espionage enforcement and increasingly constrained foreign reporting, including the withholding and revocation of visas for US journalists. Yet on the ground, another story is unfolding. When it comes to its relationship with the rest of the world, Beijing increasingly appears to be betting on direct exposure: come to China and judge for yourself. Zichen Wang is deputy secretary-general at the Center for China and Globalization, a thinktank in Beijing. This article was co-written by Hao Wu, an assistant professor at the School of International Studies at Peking University Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? body.zh: 通过放宽签证规定，北京有两件事要考虑——提振经济和改善自我形象。今天漫步在北京市中心，一件事很快就会变得显而易见：外国人回来了。他们在故宫外拍照，坐在鼓楼和三里屯周围的咖啡馆里。这种转变在网上也可见一斑。 YouTube 上越来越多地充斥着标题为“中国让我震惊”或“我在中国的第一周”的视频。大多数创作者都是游客，而不是中国专家或记者，而且他们中的许多人都是第一次接触这个国家。这种复苏令人震惊，因为对许多外部观察家来说，中国的故事已经变成了封闭和安全增强的故事 — — 与西方的战略竞争加剧、反间谍执法扩大以及对外报道日益受到限制，包括扣留和吊销美国记者的签证。然而，在地面上，另一个故事正在上演。当谈到与世界其他国家的关系时，北京似乎越来越倾向于直接曝光：来中国自己判断。王子晨是北京智库中国与全球化智库的副秘书长。本文由北京大学国际关系学院助理教授吴浩共同撰写，您对本文提出的问题有何看法？如果您想通过电子邮件提交最多 300 字的回复，以便考虑在我们的信件部分发布，请单击此处。继续阅读...

This echoes a deeper human longing to dismantle barriers and foster connection, reminding us that Yahweh desires for dividing walls of hostility to be broken down. Such direct encounters, even for economic reasons, can open pathways for...
reflection.zh: 北京邀请游客“亲自评判中国”，旨在弥合理解和认知上的鸿沟。这呼应了人类拆除隔阂、促进联结的深层渴望，提醒我们雅伟渴望拆毁敌意的隔墙。即使是出于经济原因，这种直接的接触也能为各民族之间更深的相互理解开辟道路。

verse.textEn: For he himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility.
verse.textZh: 因他使我们和睦，将两下合而为一，拆毁了中间隔断的墙。

title.en: Trump alleges China meddled in 2020 election and questions voting security ahead of midterms
title.zh: 特朗普在中期选举前指控美国选举安全存在“令人震惊的漏洞”

summary.en: The president has made claims about China's interference in the 2020 US election, which contradict previous findings from US intelligence agencies. These allegations come as the country prepares for upcoming midterm elections.
summary.zh: 总统声称中国干预了2020年美国大选，这与美国情报机构此前的调查结果直接矛盾。这些指控是在该国准备中期选举之际提出的。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has delivered a primetime address in which he accused China of interfering in the 2020 election and alleged "shocking vulnerabilities" in American voting systems.

Trump, who spoke from the White House on Thursday, has repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims about voter fraud and foreign meddling in the 2020 election, which he lost to Joe Biden.

In the half-hour speech, delivered three months before the midterm elections, he said he had declassified hundreds of intelligence files which supported his claims that Beijing had tried to sway the election in Biden's favour.

The US intelligence community has previously concluded China did not interfere in the 2020 election.

In response to his speech, China's foreign ministry strongly denied the allegations of Chinese meddling in the 2020 presidential election, saying they were "entirely fabricated".

Trump's claims are "malicious smears" which have "long been proven to be groundless", foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian said.

Trump spoke in front of several members of his top team as he gave his address, but journalists were unable to put questions to the president.

In his remarks, he accused China of the "illicit acquisition" of 220 million voter files including personal information.

Trump said voter data in 18 states was "bought, stolen or hacked by China" and accused "those responsible for sounding the alarm" of not disclosing the discovery to government officials or Congress.

A lot of voter data is publicly available , external and Trump did not in his speech present any evidence that China had used this information to alter voting systems or to influence election outcomes.

Hundreds of pages of intelligence documents were released by the White House during Trump's address, many of them heavily redacted. The BBC is in the process of reviewing them.

Democrats, meanwhile, accused Trump of attempting to sow doubts about the security of the upcoming November midterms which will decide control of Congress for the remainder of his presidency.

"Let's be clear - in America, voters choose their leaders, not the other way around," top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer posted on social media after the speech.

"Democrats will fight like hell to make sure every American voter can cast their ballot freely, without obstruction or interference from Donald Trump," he added.

The president's comments contradict previous US intelligence assessments. A 2021 report by the US National Intelligence Council said it had "high confidence" that China did not interfere in the 2020 presidential election.

"We assess that China did not deploy interference efforts and considered but did not deploy influence efforts intended to change the outcome of the US presidential election," the report stated.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普发表黄金时段讲话，指责中国干涉 2020 年大选，并声称美国投票系统存在“令人震惊的漏洞”。 周四在白宫发表讲话的特朗普多次就选民欺诈和外国干预 2020 年大选提出未经证实的指控，但他输给了乔·拜登。 在中期选举前三个月发表的半小时演讲中，他表示，他已经解密了数百份情报文件，这些文件支持他的说法，即北京试图影响选举，让选举有利于拜登。 美国情报界此前得出结论，中国没有干预2020年大选。 特朗普在发表讲话时在其高层团队的几名成员面前发表了讲话，但记者无法向总统提问。 他在讲话中指责中国“非法获取”包括个人信息在内的2.2亿份选民档案。 特朗普表示，18个州的选民数据“被中国购买、窃取或黑客入侵”，并指责“那些负责发出警报的人”没有向政府官员或国会披露这一发现。 特朗普没有提供证据证明中国利用其据称收集的信息来改变投票制度或影响选举结果。 作为对他讲话的回应，中国驻华盛顿大使馆告诉路透社，北京“从来没有也永远不会干预总统选举”。 BBC已联系中国外交部征求评论。 与此同时，民主党人指责特朗普试图对即将到来的 11 月中期选举的安全性产生怀疑，这次中期选举将决定他在总统任期剩余时间内对国会的控制权。 “让我们明确一点——在美国，选民选择他们的领导人，而不是相反，”参议院民主党领袖查克·舒默在演讲后在社交媒体上发帖称。 他补充说：“民主党人将竭尽全力确保每个美国选民都能自由投票，而不受唐纳德·特朗普的阻挠或干涉。” 总统的评论与美国之前的情报评估相矛盾。美国国家情报委员会2021年的一份报告称，“高度确信”中国没有干预2020年总统选举。 报告称：“我们评估认为，中国没有部署干预行动，并考虑过但没有部署旨在改变美国总统选举结果的影响力。” 报告称，这可能是因为中国“不认为任何一项选举结果都具有足够的优势，让中国在被抓到时冒着遭到反击的风险”。 特朗普在《华盛顿邮报》益普索公布的最新民意调查结果公布后发表了白宫讲话，该民意调查显示，许多选民对他的支持率已降至37%……

reflection.en: In a world grappling with conflicting narratives, the call to "put away falsehood and speak the truth" remains vital. When leaders make claims that contradict established intelligence, it underscores the importance of seeking truth and maintaining integrity in public discourse. Yahweh desires that our words build trust and clarity, especially in matters...
reflection.zh: 在一个充斥着相互矛盾叙述的世界里，“所以你们要弃绝谎言，各人与邻舍说实话”的呼召至关重要。当领导人发表与既定情报相悖的言论时，这凸显了在公共话语中寻求真相和保持诚信的重要性。雅伟渴望我们的言语能建立信任和清晰，尤其是在影响国家福祉的事务上。

verse.textEn: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to your neighbor.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要弃绝谎言，各人与邻舍说实话。

title.en: China: Landslide buries buildings, traps people
title.zh: 中国：山体滑坡掩埋建筑，多人被困

summary.en: A landslide in southwest China has resulted in at least 8 reported deaths and 34 people missing. Rescue operations are currently underway in the affected area.
summary.zh: 中国西南部发生山体滑坡，据报道已造成至少8人死亡，另有34人失踪。目前，受灾地区的救援行动仍在进行中。

body.zh: 官方媒体报道称，中国西南部发生山体滑坡，造成至少 8 人死亡，另有 34 人失踪。救援工作正在进行中。 据国营新华社报道，周五上午，中国重庆市附近的彭水县的一段山坡崩塌，掩埋了几栋住宅楼，造成至少八人死亡，并被困人数不明。 来自国家电视台中央电视台的图像显示，救援人员正在清理现场的大量岩石和碎片，该地点位于乌江边的一个陡坡上。 据中央电视台报道，到目前为止，至少有 10 人已从废墟中获救，没有受伤。 搜救行动正在进行中。 当地时间上午 8 点（世界标准时间 0000）左右，一名社区工作人员注意到散落的落石，随后山体滑坡发生前发布了紧急警报。当局已下令 60 多名居民撤离，但山体滑坡于上午 9 点发生，疏散工作尚未完全完成。 中国应急管理部在一份声明中表示，已部署 100 名救援人员和数十辆车辆前往现场。 这次山体滑坡是由降雨引发的，发生在乌江的一段附近，乌江穿过喀斯特山脉，沿河修建了小镇和梯田。 彭水县位于重庆直辖市东南部，与湖北省、贵州省接壤。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间点击此处并点击“星标”或“首选”按钮，将我们选为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

Psalm 46:1 reminds us that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble, offering solace and steadfast presence amidst the chaos and grief. Even as rescue efforts continue, we can hold onto the hope that divine...
reflection.zh: 在这场毁灭性的山体滑坡之后，生命逝去，许多人失踪，我们的心为受影响的人们感到悲痛。诗篇46:1提醒我们，雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助，在混乱和悲伤中提供慰藉和坚定的同在。即使救援工作仍在进行，我们也可以抱持希望，相信神圣的力量会临到那些哀伤的人和那些努力救援的人。

title.en: Xi Jinping calls for international cooperation in AI development at WAIC in Shanghai
title.zh: 习近平在上海世界人工智能大会上呼吁加强人工智能国际合作

summary.en: Chinese President Xi Jinping attended the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai, where he outlined China's approach to AI diplomacy, aiming to challenge the United States' leadership in the artificial intelligence sector.
summary.zh: 中国国家主席习近平出席了在上海举行的世界人工智能大会（WAIC），他在会上阐述了中国的人工智能外交愿景，旨在挑战美国在该领域的主导地位。

body.en:
Xi Jinping marked his first in-person attendance at the World ​Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai, where he shared China's vision of AI diplomacy to challenge US dominance in the sector.

China's President  Xi Jinping  has called for global cooperation on  artificial intelligence (AI)  development, telling a major Shanghai forum that no single country should dominate the AI industry.

Xi on Friday delivered a keynote address at the opening event of the World ​Artificial ‌Intelligence Conference (WAIC), which he was attending for the first time, underpinning AI's growing strategic importance for China.

"AI development should not be a solo performance by a single country, but a symphony of international cooperation," Xi said at the gathering.

To prevent the creation of what he called "new ​historical injustices" ​in AI, Xi promoted Beijing's role in ensuring equitable access for developing countries to AI capacity building.

He announced China's plans to cooperate with several international bodies, including from Asia, Africa, Latin America and BRICS  nations to provide opportunities in the AI domain.

On Thursday, representatives from 29 nations inked an agreement to establish ​the World AI Cooperation Organization, headquartered in Shanghai, China's Xinhua news agency reported.

The signatory nations included Russia, Belarus, ⁠Serbia, Cuba, Brazil and Venezuela, along with 12 Asian and 10 African countries.

China says the intergovernmental body aims to promote international cooperation and global ​governance in AI.

Xi also stressed the importance of a "people-centered" approach in the development of AI technology.

"We should put in place laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning, and emergency response systems, in order to ... ensure AI is always under human control," the Chinese leader said.

The conference comes as China and the United States prepare for their first government-level AI talks under US President Donald Trump's administration. 

Chinese AI models are attracting global users with lower costs as they catch up to the more expensive US AI offerings.

The United States and European Union have imposed curbs on tech imports from China, citing national security concerns.

There are also growing concerns over the deployment of AI on the battlefield and its use by hackers and terrorists.

"We should jointly oppose overstretching the national security concept in the field of AI or placing one country's security over that of others," Xi said on Friday.

The WAIC lasts for four days and features over 1,000 exhibitors from Chinese tech firms alongside officials and researchers.

title.en: 'Shocking vulnerabilities': Trump makes sweeping claims China meddled in US elections
title.zh: “令人震惊的漏洞”：特朗普就中国干预美国大选发表全面声明

summary.en: The US president made broad election security claims, laying groundwork for the federal government to take action.

body.en:
In a speech attacking US election integrity on Friday, US President Donald Trump released intelligence that he said showed major Chinese interference in US elections, reviving his false claims he won the 2020 election.

Trump's allegations about the "shocking vulnerabilities" in the American electoral system appeared to lay the groundwork for the Republican to dispute the results of November's crucial US midterm elections .

It underscored Trump's effort to make election security a central political issue ahead of November's midterm vote, when Republicans in Congress will face the prospect of losing control of both the House of Representatives and Senate — an outcome that would carry significant political consequences for Trump.

"We can never watch a stolen election again," Trump said in the primetime address, referencing his 2020 presidential election defeat by Democrat Joe Biden.

Trump said he was declassifying huge amounts of intelligence data that showed, among other things, that superpower rival China had illicitly acquired 220 million US voter files.

"Over a period of years, starting during the 2020 election cycle, the People's Republic of China carried out what is believed to be the largest compromise of election data in history," Trump said in the televised speech from the White House.

He asserted that members of the US intelligence community deliberately suppressed information about the extent of China's activities.

His allegations contradict an unclassified 2021 US intelligence community assessment that found no indications any foreign actor tried to alter or succeeded in altering "any technical aspect" of the 2020 presidential election vote.

The assessment was conducted under John Ratcliffe, then Trump's director of national intelligence and now his CIA director.

Trump also claimed there were more than 250,000 non-US citizens registered to vote in four states.

Trump has persistently claimed his 2020 election defeat was "rigged," although more than 60 lawsuits produced no ruling establishing fraud capable of changing the outcome, while recounts, audits and his own justice department found none.

After railing against election security in the 25-minute address, Trump pressed Republicans in Congress to pass his signature elections legislation, the SAVE America Act, which has been stalled for months.

It seeks to impose new voter identification and citizenship requirements, despite longstanding findings that voter fraud in US elections is rare.

Election security experts have said these measures would make it harder for millions of eligible voters to cast a ballot.

title.en: Philippines condemns monkey video on Chinese media as racist
title.zh: 菲律宾谴责中国媒体上的“猴子视频”为种族主义

summary.en: An AI-generated video circulated on Chinese media, depicting a monkey in Philippine attire singing about claims to the South China Sea, has been condemned by the Philippines as racist.
summary.zh: 中国媒体上流传的一段人工智能视频，展示了一只身着菲律宾服装的猴子演唱其对南海的主张，菲律宾谴责该视频具有种族主义色彩。

body.en:
The Philippines has condemned the "dehumanising and racist" portrayal of the country as a timid monkey strong-armed by the US and Japan to take Beijing on over the South China Sea .

Last week, China Daily posted an AI-generated video featuring a monkey in a Filipino shirt. It screams as arms bearing the Japanese and US flags shove it onto a rickety karaoke stage set up in a boat.

After it gets scolded for singing the wrong song, it pulls out a sheet reading "South China Sea arbitration award". It is then flung into the sea and blasted by a water cannon.

Tense stand-offs and occasional violent confrontations between Philippine and Chinese vessels in the disputed waters have grown in recent years.

At the centre of tensions between Manila and Beijing are the Spratly Islands and Scarborough Shoal (known as Huangyan Island in China), a little more than 100 miles (160km) from the Philippines and 500 miles from China.

The Chinese Coast Guard routinely uses high-pressure water cannons against Philippine vessels in the disputed shoals, which have led to damage and injuries.

"Disagreement over legal and political issues does not justify resorting to disturbing imagery, which has no place in the civil public discourse of a responsible state," Manila's foreign ministry said, demanding that the clip be removed.

"Such imagery and misinformation only serve to widen the distrust between the Philippines and China," it added.

The Philippine defence ministry called the video "contemptible propaganda", saying it "exposes the moral and intellectual bankruptcy of China's propaganda machine".

"The recent spate of schizophrenic behaviour of the Chinese Communist Party is too clear to disregard or ignore," defence secretary Gilbert Teodoro said.

The video, posted on 10 July, remains on China Daily's Facebook page at time of writing.

The past week marks a decade since the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled in favour of the Philippines, concluding that China's expansive claims in the South China Sea had no legal basis under international law.

Tensions between Beijing and Manila have sharply escalated in recent years due to their overlapping claims, with each side accusing the other of provocations and altercations at sea, including some involving weapons such as swords, spears and knives.

In June, Beijing installed a floating barrier at the entrance to the Scarborough Shoal that was removed after the Philippines filed formal diplomatic protests.

Also in June, China barred Teodoro, Manila's defence secretary, and his immediate family from entering mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau.

China Daily's caption to its post of the monkey clip reiterates Bejing's position.

title.en: Albanese issues Opposition a One Nation 'test' at launch of Islamophobia report response

summary.en: Prime Minister Albanese has challenged Opposition Leader Angus Taylor on his approach to Pauline Hanson, leader of One Nation, following the release of a response to an Islamophobia report. Albanese urged Taylor to emulate former prime minister John Howard's handling of Hanson.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has issued a "test" to Opposition leader Angus Taylor, saying he should rule out any future political deals with One Nation.

While speaking about the government's plan to combat Islamophobia on Saturday, Albanese was asked by a reporter if One Nation leader Pauline Hanson's comments about the Muslim community were a "threat to social cohesion".

Albanese said Hanson had been "undermining social cohesion" since she entered the 1996 federal election as a Liberal Party candidate.

"The Liberal Party at that time disendorsed Ms Hanson and dissociated themselves from her and indeed then refused to give preferences to One Nation," he added.

"The test for Angus Taylor is: Will he rule out preference deals and arrangements with One Nation going forward?"

Albanese also said Taylor should reverse course on adopting "One Nation-lite" policies and return to the centre of politics.

The prime minister made the comments when issuing the government's official response to a set of recommendations put forward by Special Envoy to Combat Islamophobia, Aftab Malik, in his landmark report submitted last year .

On Saturday, the Albanese government accepted 35 of the 54 recommendations — 10 months after Malik's report was handed down.

It comes a day after the release of a controversial podcast interview between Hanson and far-right UK figure Tommy Robinson, in which Hanson lamented the end of the White Australia policy.

Asked by Robinson how Australia had ended up with "Pakistanis, Somalis, all of these African problems with violent Africans," Hanson said it started with the end of the White Australia Policy.

The postwar wave of migrants was different to today's situation because the new arrivals "really assimilated' and "learned to speak English", she said.

Albanese also addressed those comments on Saturday, saying it was important to remember that the White Australia policy began to be dismantled under the leadership of Liberal prime minister Harold Holt.

"The movement away from the White Australia policy wasn't just the Labor government of Gough Whitlam, it was actually a bipartisan position that began in the 1960s.

In the interview with Robinson, Hanson also claimed people in 'Muslim areas' were taking advantage of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS).

Gamel Kheir from the Lebanese Muslim Association said he wasn't surprised by Hanson's comments.

"We're quite used to that dog-whistling racist rhetoric now. It's beyond being alarmed," Kheir told SBS News.

reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到管家责任、供应与公共福祉。1 Peter 4:10提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以服事邻舍的好管家心态来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: ‘It’s only going to get worse’: wildfires forcing firefighters to make impossible choices
title.zh: “只会变得更糟”：野火迫使消防员做出不可能的选择

summary.en: Wildfires, intensified by the climate crisis, are spreading to new regions, compelling firefighters to ration resources and make difficult decisions about which blazes to prioritize. Experts warn that the situation is expected to worsen, placing increasing strain on emergency services.
summary.zh: 受气候危机加剧影响，野火正蔓延至新的地区，迫使消防员不得不分配有限的资源，艰难地决定优先扑灭哪些火灾。专家警告称，情况预计将进一步恶化，给应急服务带来更大压力。

body.en: As the climate crisis fuels more intense blazes, pushing them to new parts of the world, those tackling them are forced to ration resources and decide which to fight César Alcaraz had only just become a firefighter in the late 1990s when he found himself ambushed by a fast-moving blaze. Barely able to breathe and with no more water left in his truck, he and his colleagues fled an inferno ravaging Spain’s Montgó mountain region, wishing their bosses had sent more support. But nearly three decades on, as an officer with Alicante’s provincial firefighters, Alcaraz has more sympathy for the agonising choices that commanders have to make. When wildfires overwhelm an area, his job resembles that of a doctor in an emergency room with too few ventilators. Continue reading...
body.zh: 随着气候危机引发更猛烈的火灾，将火势推向世界新的地区，应对这些问题的人们被迫配给资源并决定扑灭哪些火势。塞萨尔·阿尔卡拉斯 (César Alcaraz) 在 20 世纪 90 年代末才刚刚成为一名消防员，就发现自己遭到了一场快速蔓延的大火的伏击。他和同事们几乎无法呼吸，卡车里也没有水了，他们逃离了肆虐西班牙蒙戈山区的大火，希望他们的老板能提供更多支持。但近三十年后，作为阿利坎特省消防队员的一名警官，阿尔卡拉兹对指挥官必须做出的痛苦选择更加同情。当野火淹没一个地区时，他的工作就像是呼吸机太少的急诊室里的医生。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The escalating climate crisis is forcing firefighters to make agonizing decisions about resource allocation, highlighting the immense pressure on those on the front lines. In moments when human wisdom feels insufficient to navigate such impossible choices, we are reminded of the need for divine guidance. Yahweh promises to generously grant wisdom to those...
reflection.zh: 气候危机日益加剧，迫使消防员在资源分配上面临痛苦的抉择，这凸显了前线人员所承受的巨大压力。在人类智慧不足以应对这些不可能的选择时，我们被提醒需要雅伟的指引。雅伟应许慷慨地赐予那些求告祂的人智慧，即使在压倒性的挑战中也能带来清晰和力量。

verse.textEn: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.
verse.textZh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神，主就必赐给他。

title.en: Hanson ‘undermining social cohesion’, Albanese says, as Labor responds to Islamophobia envoy’s report
title.zh: 阿尔巴尼斯称汉森“破坏社会凝聚力”，工党回应伊斯兰恐惧症特使报告

summary.en: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has accused Pauline Hanson of “undermining social cohesion” in response to a report by the Islamophobia envoy, Aftab Malik. The government is implementing 54 recommendations, including forming a new education taskforce and a federal police social cohesion team.

body.en: Government’s response to 54 recommendations made by Aftab Malik includes new education taskforce and federal police social cohesion team Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Anthony Albanese has accused Pauline Hanson of “undermining social cohesion” after his Islamophobia envoy warned the One Nation leader’s words could have violent consequences. The government formally responded on Saturday to the 54 recommendations made by the special envoy to combat Islamophobia, Aftab Malik, in his report handed down 10 months ago. Continue reading...
