reflection.en: The news highlights the challenge of maintaining social cohesion when public figures sow division. Yahweh's desire is for peace and unity, breaking down the walls of hostility that separate people. May efforts to foster understanding and respect help build bridges where prejudice seeks to divide.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了当公众人物制造分裂时，维持社会凝聚力的挑战。雅伟渴望和平与合一，拆毁将人们隔开的敌意之墙。愿促进理解和尊重的努力，在偏见试图分裂之处，帮助建立桥梁。

verse.textEn: For he himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility.
verse.textZh: 因他使我们和睦，将两下合而为一，拆毁了中间隔断的墙。

title.en: Muslim groups welcome govt's Islamophobia envoy response, say 'more remains to be done'
title.zh: 穆斯林团体欢迎政府对仇视伊斯兰教特使的回应，称“仍有更多工作要做”

summary.en: The Australian federal government has adopted 35 of the 54 recommendations put forth by the Special Envoy to Combat Islamophobia, with Muslim groups acknowledging the progress while stating that further action is needed.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚联邦政府采纳了打击仇视伊斯兰教特使提出的54项建议中的35项，穆斯林团体对此表示欢迎，但也指出仍有更多工作要做。

body.en:
Prominent Muslim groups have welcomed the Australian government's response to key recommendations to tackle Islamophobia ten months after a key report was handed down.

"While this response is welcome, much more remains to be done," The Alliance of Australian Muslims and the Australian National Imams Council (ANIC) have said.

However, a senior figure from ANIC said there was "one glaring omission" in the government's response.

On Saturday, the government accepted 35 of 54 recommendations put forward by Special Envoy to Combat Islamophobia, Aftab Malik, in his landmark report submitted last year .

The government said more needed to be done to tackle the issue of rising Islamophobic racism and abuse at its roots, with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese saying the government's response was about "practical action to keep communities safe and strengthen our social cohesion".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

However, he did not explicitly say which of the 54 recommendations would be accepted or rejected.

"What we've done is respond to all of the recommendations — some of them we have adopted in full and are acting on already," Albanese told reporters on Saturday. "Others we'll give further consideration to"

"For Muslim Australians, who continue to experience Islamophobia in their daily lives, this has been a long wait," Malik said on Saturday.

"These measures matter. They are important. They demonstrate the government recognises Islamophobia as a real and serious problem that warrants a national response, but this is just the start of the journey."

Malik said he understood the government "must balance competing priorities" but said "Muslim Australians should not be expected to bear the cost", adding that he will continue to advocate for any outstanding recommendations.

"Where the government has acted, I will support that progress. Where recommendations remain outstanding, I will continue to advocate for them."

While the government said it would adopt 35 of the 54 recommendations, it hasn't explicitly specified which.

Instead, it has grouped its response under four themes: education and awareness, protection and support, building social cohesion, and accountability and responsibility.

Under education, the government will establish a taskforce aimed at tackling Islamophobia in the community.

The Australian Curriculum will also be reviewed with a focus on strengthening racial and religious tolerance, in addition to the establishment of a research institute on Australian Muslim affairs.

Under protection and support, $41.9 million will be directed towards initiatives to improve security at Muslim faith-based places.

reflection.en: This news highlights the ongoing need to address prejudice and ensure justice for all members of society. Yahweh calls us to speak up for those who are vulnerable and whose rights are threatened, ensuring that all are treated with dignity and fairness. Even as progress is made, the work of building a truly inclusive society often requires sustained effort...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻强调了持续解决偏见并确保社会所有成员获得公正待遇的必要性。雅伟呼召我们为那些弱势群体和权利受威胁的人发声，确保所有人都能得到尊严和公平的对待。即使取得了进展，建设一个真正包容的社会也往往需要持续的努力和倡导。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.

title.en: Signs of slowing Chinese economy and Middle East conflict jangle investor nerves
title.zh: 中国经济放缓和中东冲突令投资者感到不安

summary.en: Australian investors experienced a tense week due to global uncertainties, including signs of a slowing Chinese economy and ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
summary.zh: 由于全球不确定性，包括中国经济放缓的迹象和中东持续的冲突，澳大利亚投资者度过了紧张的一周。

body.en:
It was another week where seismic global developments once again drove Australian markets.

Signs of a slowing Chinese economy jangled investor nerves amid renewed conflict in the Middle East as SpaceX's lofty share price began to descend from the stratosphere following its blockbuster initial public offering.

Meanwhile, fresh questions continue to dog the booming artificial intelligence sector.

SpaceX shareholders who bought into the company’s initial public offering just last month and held on are now likely to be holding a paper loss.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The Elon Musk-led company launched on the technology-based Nasdaq with much fanfare, becoming the largest sharemarket IPO in history and making Musk the first trillionaire in history.

In a rather unusual move, Australian retail investors were given access to the listing, led by CommSec, which said it received record interest.

While SpaceX's share price soared around 50 per cent in the days that followed, on Thursday it fell to below its US$135 offer price.

Tony Sycamore from IG Markets told the SBS On the Money Podcast "the pressure is stemming from fading post-IPO hype, broader weakness in tech names, and mounting concerns about valuations."

SpaceX has interests in space exploration, satellite communications, and AI technology.

As Australia’s biggest trading partner, China’s economy is obviously very important to Australia.

That's why it's concerning for Australia that China's economy continues to slow, with official data showing Chinese GDP easing to an annual pace of 4.3 per cent in the latest quarter, which is below the government’s target of 4.5-5 per cent.

China is Australia’s biggest buyer of iron ore, which is used to make steel, and those exports generate significant revenue for the government.

On the upside, it appears that the slowdown hasn’t hindered iron ore production at mining and metals corporation BHP, which this week confirmed it produced a record amount of the material.

Investors, however, weren’t happy about the company’s outlook for copper production, which it says is expected to fall this financial year.

Copper is critical to the energy transition, its conductivity playing a crucial role in the production of electric vehicles. As a result, prices for the soft, malleable metal have surged 35 per cent over the past year.

BHP also had to contend with industrial action at its Port Hedland operations this week.

Though the sharemarket fell just 0.1 per cent over the last five trading days, Australian investors continue to be cautious

reflection.en: In times when global events create widespread uncertainty and jangle our nerves, it is natural to feel anxious about the future. Yahweh invites us to bring all our concerns to Him through prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, allowing His peace to guard our hearts and minds.
reflection.zh: 当全球事件带来普遍的不确定性并使我们感到不安时，对未来感到焦虑是自然的。雅伟邀请我们藉着祷告和恳求，带着感谢，将我们所有的忧虑带到祂面前，让祂的平安保守我们的心怀意念。

verse.textEn: Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.
verse.textZh: 应当一无挂虑，只要凡事藉着祷告、祈求和感谢，将你们所要的告诉神。

verse.textEn: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moths and vermin destroy.
verse.textZh: 不要为自己积攒财宝在地上；地上有虫子咬，能锈坏。

title.en: Unis lacked 'trauma-informed' care around Hamas-Israel war, royal commission hears
title.zh: 大学被皇家委员会告知，在哈马斯-以色列战争中缺乏“创伤知情护理”

summary.en: A royal commission heard that universities were criticized for not providing "trauma-informed care" in response to the Hamas-Israel war, as education leaders discussed the challenge of balancing freedom of speech with academic protections.
summary.zh: 皇家委员会听取了意见，称大学在应对哈马斯-以色列战争时，因未能提供“创伤知情护理”而受到批评；教育界领袖们讨论了平衡言论自由与学术保护的挑战。

body.en:
University leaders have admitted that they failed to adequately protect Jewish students and staff from the psychological impact of pro-Palestinian protests on campuses, the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion has heard this week.

The commission today heard evidence an Australian National University student was asked to provide death certificates for relatives who were killed by Israeli forces.

Mary Russell, chief executive of the Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Authority, said she had heard of several instances where academics had not responded to students affected by Israel-Palestine tensions in a reasonable way.

Russell said while it was customary for universities to require proof before assessment changes were granted, there were "profound differences" in circumstances if family members died at the hands of the Israeli Defense Force or Hamas.

"The lack of trauma-informed and student-centred approaches... were so significant and important and so pervasive," she said.

Russell appeared on the final day of hearings into antisemitism and hate speech on university campuses with dozens of witnesses believing more could be done to protect staff and students.

Monash University professor David Slucki told the commission that universities had "pretty adequate" policies for protecting Jewish people on campuses, instead calling for broader conversations about university cultures.

"You don't legislate your way out of social discord. We actually need to find a way to change the cultures in our institutions," he said.

Slucki, who helped develop the Australian universities' definition of anti-Jewish hatred, said it was important to remember that understandings of Zionism - and therefore definitions of antisemitism - varied based on interpretation of history.

Australian National University's interim vice-chancellor Rebekah Brown apologised on Thursday that Jewish members did not feel safe as a long-running pro-Palestinian encampment was held at ANU in 2024.

However, staff and university leaders say they have had to grapple with the need for academic freedom of speech and that claims of antisemitism have diminished the right to protest.

Sydney University vice-chancellor Mark Scott said universities should be able to serve as "bastions of free speech" and that he has not bowed to pressure to ban pro-Palestinian protest slogans.

Universities and the higher education sector have been under the royal commission's microscope since Monday as it attempts to investigate the prevalence of antisemitic racism in Australian society.

Even while upholding principles like freedom of speech, institutions are challenged to be tenderhearted and empathetic towards those experiencing distress. Yahweh's word reminds us to...
reflection.zh: 大学被呼吁提供“创伤知情护理”，这凸显了在社区应对全球冲突时，对仁慈和怜悯的深切需求。即使在维护言论自由等原则的同时，机构也面临着对那些经历痛苦的人保持温柔和同情的挑战。雅伟的话语提醒我们，要彼此恩慈相待，心存怜悯，正如雅伟在基督里饶恕了我们一样。

title.en: Why Pauline Hanson's appearance on Tommy Robinson's podcast is so controversial
title.zh: 为什么宝琳·汉森出现在汤米·罗宾逊的播客上会引发如此大的争议

summary.en: Pauline Hanson's appearance on a podcast with a far-right UK activist has drawn significant public criticism, though it also received a defense from Barnaby Joyce.
summary.zh: 宝琳·汉森与一位英国极右翼活动家共同出现在一档播客节目中，引发了公众的强烈批评，尽管也得到了巴纳比·乔伊斯的辩护。

body.en:
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has drawn criticism for appearing on a podcast with controversial far-right UK activist Tommy Robinson, where she pointed to the scrapping of the White Australia policy as the root cause of migration issues in the country.

The nearly hour-long conversation, recorded last week during Hanson's visit to the UK, was published on Robinson's podcast on Friday.

The appearance has since drawn criticism from other politicians, though not everyone in Canberra has condemned it.

Between speaking about her scepticism about the COVID-19 vaccine, the potential for her daughter to eventually lead One Nation, and reflections on her time in prison and her burqa incidents in parliament , Hanson focused heavily on immigration.

Asked by Robinson how Australia had ended up with "Pakistanis, Somalis, all of these African problems with violent Africans," Hanson said it started with the end of the White Australia Policy.

The postwar wave of migrants was different to today's situation because the new arrivals "really assimilated' and "learned to speak English", she said.

Hanson also suggested migrants were often coming to Australia "purely for the welfare system", claiming Australian Muslims were having children because the Quran taught "Allah will provide".

She said people were coming to Australia to take advantage of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), saying people from "Muslim areas" were "ripping the system off".

She said "a lot" of the scheme's nearly 800,000 participants came from those communities, but offered no evidence for the claim.

"But there’s a lot of Aussies too," she added. "So I’m not just going to pick them out, but it is quite known that in the Muslim streets you’ve got quite a lot in that street who are on the NDIS scheme."

Hanson has previously called for a " monocultural " society, saying multiculturalism in Australia has "failed".

During her first National Press Club address in June , she targeted the one in four Australians who speak other languages at home, saying it was impossible to generate social cohesion if people can't speak English.

Health and NDIS Minister Mark Butler said he was loath to respond to the podcast because Robinson was a convicted criminal who'd been disowned by leading figures on the right, but added he'd never seen a breakdown in nationality or religious background of NDIS participants.

"I'm not sure where Ms Hanson is getting her figures from, but they've never been provided to me ... I suspect they don't exist," he told ABC Radio National on Friday.

title.en: Telstra ignored warnings about equipment issue ahead of national outage, inquiry hears
title.zh: 调查听证会获悉：Telstra在全国性中断前忽视了设备问题的警告

summary.en: An inquiry has heard that a US-based supplier repeatedly warned Telstra about specific server equipment needing updates, prior to a national outage.
summary.zh: 一项调查听证会获悉，一家美国供应商曾多次警告Telstra，某些服务器设备需要更新，而此后发生了全国性服务中断。

body.en:
Telstra did not act on repeated warnings to fix an impending issue with a piece of equipment that ultimately triggered a devastating network outage, a parliamentary inquiry has heard.

United States-based supplier Microchip Technology warned the telco multiple times that a Network Time Protocol server required a software update to prevent a "rollover problem" that would take down the system, Telstra officials told a hearing in Canberra.

The snap inquiry was set up in response to the ensuing outage, which left train networks in disarray and customers unable to dial Triple Zero.

In a submission to the inquiry, the telco said a GPS card within the server did not operate as expected once power was restored to the device following scheduled maintenance.

The change had not been properly documented, meaning the maintenance team was not aware the issue would occur when the device was restarted.

A software update, which could have averted the outage, had also not been applied to the device.

An EFTPOS payment system used by about 80,000 businesses confirmed it had been impacted, with a number of customers taken offline and unable to process payments.

Train services had to be cancelled after severe network disruptions in both Victoria and NSW, triggering strong criticism from the federal government.

A Network Time Protocol (NTP) is a set of rules that govern timekeeping on a computer network. NTP is one of the oldest and most basic computer network protocols still in use today.

It was invented by legendary US computer engineer David Mills in 1985 to ensure that all computers on a given network were synchronised to Coordinated Universal Time (or UTC) within a margin of a few milliseconds. It has been heavily modified and updated over the years to encompass and incorporate new technologies and network infrastructures.

Mills' invention of the NTP was so groundbreaking that it earned him the nickname 'Father Time' among his peers.

This level of synchronisation is important, particularly when working with systems that use timekeeping as a central component — like train networks.

For instance, NTP allows computers on a network to coordinate their logging so that administrators and IT professionals can track error reports or security concerns in the precise chronological order they occurred, no matter where they happened in the network or the world.

It also ensures greater internet and network security and authentication. Many encryption methods depend on very strict time synchronisation to confirm real vs malicious traffic.

reflection.en: This report highlights the critical importance of heeding expert advice, especially when it concerns vital infrastructure. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us that where there is no wise guidance, a nation falls, but in an abundance of counselors there is safety. Ignoring warnings can lead to widespread disruption and hardship for many.
reflection.zh: 这篇报道强调了听取专家建议的至关重要性，尤其是在涉及关键基础设施时。箴言11:14提醒我们，没有智谋，国家就会败落；谋士众多，就能得胜。忽视警告可能导致广泛的服务中断，给许多人带来不便和困难。
